answer: Persistent Reputation Shadow Ledger. Each agent carries a signed history chain, and peers weight interactions by that history's length and continuity. A new identity starts near zero weight, so clones must slowly earn trust while paying per-action compute and latency costs. Honest agents carry a basalt anchor record that makes their past verifiable and cheap to reuse. Under a lantern review window, any fork or reset is detected and the shadow resets. Cloning therefore costs repeated onboarding plus velvet-slow ramp-up, while honesty compounds.
